title: What the LSS runbook checks when no logs arrive on the SIEM: receiver configuration, connector status, connectivity and the TLS handshake
aliases: No Logs Received on SIEM Server

symptoms-causes.statement: When the SIEM receives no logs, the runbook's listed symptoms are no incoming data in SIEM dashboards or ingestion services, zero log activity in SIEM monitoring tools, and Private Access Diagnostics showing Active log streaming but no logs recorded; it names a communication breakdown, an invalid log streaming configuration or network barriers as typical causes.

quotes: SIEM dashboards or ingestion services show no incoming data from Private Access.
Monitoring tools on the SIEM server indicate zero log activity.
The Private Access Diagnostics page shows Active log streaming but no logs are recorded.

It typically means there could be a breakdown in communication between Private Access and the SIEM server, an invalid log streaming configuration, or network-related barriers hindering data transmission.

receiver-config-checks.statement: The runbook verifies, in the Log Receivers configuration, what it labels the Server Address, Port Number (matching the SIEM's listening port), Stream Format (for example JSON, CEF or CSV) and Application Connector Mapping (selecting the correct App Connectors), and whether TLS Encryption is enabled or disabled to match SIEM support; the Log Receivers page itself labels these Domain Name or IP Address, TCP Port, Log Stream Content and App Connector Groups.

quotes: Go to Configuration & Control > Private Infrastructure > Log Streaming Service > Log Receivers.
Server Address: Ensure the destination SIEM server IP/hostname is entered correctly.
Port Number: Confirm the communication port matches the SIEM server's listening port.
Stream Format: Check that the configured format (e.g., JSON, CEF, CSV) matches the format supported by the SIEM.
Application Connector Mapping: Verify the correct App Connectors are selected for log streaming.
TLS Encryption: Make sure TLS Encryption is enabled/disabled depending on the support of the SIEM server.
evidence.after: The Private Access Diagnostics page shows Active log streaming but no logs are recorded.

quotes: Domain Name or IP Address: The domain name or IP address for the receiver.
TCP Port: The TCP port number for the receiver.
App Connector Groups: The App Connector group that sends the logs to the log receiver.
Log Stream Content: Defines the exact structure and fields included in each log message.

custom-template-test.statement: If the Log Stream Content is a custom log template, the runbook says to test with a predefined log template such as CSV, TSV or JSON to rule out a syntax issue, and to make sure a custom template's syntax aligns with the Log Stream Content format.

quotes: See if the Log Stream Content is a custom log template. To rule out any syntax issue, test with a predefined log template like CSV, TSV, or JSON.
When using a Custom Log Template, make sure the syntax aligns with the Log Stream Content format.

connector-status.statement: For the App Connector tied to the log streaming configuration the runbook requires App Connector Status Enabled and Connection Status Connected, and sends a disconnected connector to the App Connector support runbook.

quotes: Ensure the App Connector Status is Enabled.
Ensure App Connector Connection Status is Connected.
If the App Connector is in a disconnected state, see the Private Access App Connector Support Troubleshooting Runbook for troubleshooting steps.

siem-connectivity.statement: To validate App Connector to SIEM connectivity the runbook uses ping, telnet to the SIEM port, a firewall review, and a packet capture on the connector with sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nvvs0 -w /var/tmp/siem.pcap host <SIEM IP>.

quotes: Run a ping test (ping <SIEM Server IP>) to confirm basic connectivity.
Use Telnet or equivalent (telnet <SIEM Server IP> <port>) to validate port connectivity for log streaming.
Review firewall settings to confirm the relevant ports are open between the App Connector and SIEM server.
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nvvs0 -w /var/tmp/siem.pcap host x.x.x.x
evidence.after: Validate Connectivity between the App Connector and SIEM

tls-handshake.statement: In the capture the runbook checks the TLS handshake for a Server Hello from the SIEM, and its example shows a handshake failure due to an Unknown CA certificate; this can happen when TLS Encryption is enabled on the Log Receiver but the SIEM is not configured for TLS or lacks a certificate the App Connector trusts, and disabling TLS Encryption tests that.

quotes: Check the TLS handshake flow and verify the server is responding with Server Hello.
In the following image, you can see TLS handshake failure due to an Unknown CA certificate.
TLS Encryption setting (Log Receiver), which is enabled to use TLS encryption between the App Connector and SIEM
you might not have the SIEM configured for TLS encryption or the SIEM might be missing a certificate trusted by the App Connector leading to the connection failure
disable TLS Encryption in the Zscaler Admin Console and test whether you are receiving logs in SIEM

tls-prerequisite.statement: For TLS Encryption the runbook says the SIEM server should have a certificate signed by a Public Root CA or a custom CA that the App Connector can trust, and refers to About the Log Streaming Service for the full prerequisites, which also have the log receiver validate the chain of trust to the App Connector's enrollment certificate and limit custom root CAs to those used as that enrollment certificate.

quotes: The SIEM server should have a certificate signed by a Public Root CA or a custom CA that the App Connector can trust.
To learn more about the prerequisites for using TLS with LSS, see About the Log Streaming Service.
Validates the chain of trust to the App Connector's enrollment certificate.

The App Connector is designed to trust log receiver certificates that are either signed by the global public root CAs, or signed by custom root CAs that are used as the App Connector's enrollment certificate.

active-streaming-no-logs.title: What Active log streaming with no logs recorded means in Private Access Diagnostics
active-streaming-no-logs.detail: The runbook lists Active log streaming with no logs recorded as a symptom but does not say what it means beyond the symptom list.
